tools.name: list_browsers
tools.description: List the shared browsers: name, kind (launched: a headless Chromium code-browser runs; attached: the user's own browser, which a human attached in the panel), status (running|stopped, or connecting for an attached one), who controls it (agent|human), the CDP endpoint while running, the read-only allowUnsandboxed (whether a human allowed it to run without the sandbox), and for an attached browser `attached` (its debug address, how it is reached, and whether Chrome asks the user to approve each connection).

tools.name: start_browser
tools.description: Start (creating on first use) a persistent headless Chromium that you and the human share. Workflow: start_browser -> read the returned snippet -> run it via Bash as an .mjs script (it connects to the browser over CDP with Playwright; the browser and its tabs keep state between scripts). The project needs no Playwright install. A browser name keeps its logins and cookies across stops. The page's viewport height follows the human's panel shape (launched browsers), so read innerHeight instead of assuming it. The human watches and can take control in a panel: obey `controller` in the result, and while it is "human" do not drive the page, call browser_info again later. When the host has no usable Chromium sandbox the start is refused with SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE unless a human has turned on "Allow without sandbox" for that browser in the panel; you cannot turn it on, so ask the user. Check `sandbox` in the result and do not browse untrusted pages when it is false. An attached browser (the user's own, which a human attached in the panel) cannot be started or reconnected by you: start_browser refuses it with ATTACHED and the panel path, so ask the user to press Connect there.

name.description: Browser name (lowercase letters, digits, dashes). Defaults to "default".

tools.name: stop_browser
tools.description: Stop a shared browser. Its profile (logins, cookies) is kept; start_browser brings it back. For an attached browser (the user's own) it only disconnects code-browser: the browser and its tabs keep running, and only the user can reconnect it.

tools.name: browser_info
tools.description: Current state of a running shared browser: CDP endpoint, open tabs, the active tab, and who controls it. Returns a ready-to-run Playwright snippet and the panel path to give the user. The page's viewport height follows the human's panel shape (launched browsers). Call it before each script: if controller is "human" the human has taken over, so do not drive the page until it is "agent" again. The browser may run unsandboxed where a human allowed it (read-only `allowUnsandboxed`): check `sandbox`. `kind` is attached for the user's own browser: work in your own tab there, and when `attached.asksApproval` is true, Chrome asks the user to allow every script's connection, so tell them before each script.
